result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.select_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select nodes using a predicate function. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5469-L5514){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_nodes(predicate) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Applies a custom filter function to all nodes, selecting those for which the predicate returns `True`. The predicate receives a `Node` object with properties: `id`, `label`, and attributes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [predicate]{.doc-parameter-name} : Function that takes a `Node` object and returns `bool`. Should return `True` to select the nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Select nodes by attribute value: ::: {#04510249 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", type="hub", score=10) .add_node(label="B", type="leaf", score=5) .add_node(label="C", type="hub", score=8) .select_nodes(lambda n: n.attributes.get("type") == "hub") ) selected = graph.get_selected_node_ids() # Returns node IDs for 'A' and 'C' selected # Select nodes by ID pattern (if using integer IDs) # graph.select_nodes(lambda n: n.id > 100) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [3, 1] ``` ::: :::
